arguments.value: American International Group, Inc. (AIG) and American General Life Insurance Company of Delaware (the Company) entered into this agreement to maintain the Company’s capital. If the Company’s Total Adjusted Capital falls below a specified minimum percentage of its Company Action Level RBC for the first and third fiscal quarters, AIG must provide qualifying capital contributions within the stated time periods so the Company’s projected capital will meet the minimum. If the Company’s Total Adjusted Capital is above the specified minimum percentage for the first, second, and third fiscal quarters, and at fiscal year end, the Company must declare and pay ordinary dividends to its equity holders, subject to applicable law and approvals, in an amount designed to bring capital back down to the target level. The agreement defines the capital terms by reference to Delaware insurance law, NAIC RBC instructions if needed, and a Specified Minimum Percentage initially set at 350% of Company Action Level RBC, which is reviewed at least annually and may be revised more often if needed. AIG may make contributions directly or through the Company’s direct parent, and the Company must use best efforts to pass dividends up to AIG. The agreement requires compliance with applicable law and regulatory approvals, allows policyholders to enforce certain rights if the Company fails to act and AIG does not cure after notice, and states that the agreement is not a guarantee of the Company’s obligations or a claim on AIG’s assets. It continues indefinitely unless terminated under the agreement’s terms, is governed by New York law, and superseded the prior December 13, 1991 letter agreement effective April 24, 2011.
